newsitem.title: USA: Israeli critics disappointed with summit outcome.
newsitem.headline: Israeli critics disappointed with summit outcome.

text.p: Two Israeli politicians who are outspoken critics of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu voiced disappointment on Wednesday at outcome of the Middle East summit in Washington.

Yael Dayan, a Labour Party member of Israel's parliament, and Shulamit Aloni, a founder of the liberal Meretz Party and a former Israeli minister of communications, spoke in San Francisco where they are attending the "State of the World Forum," a gathering of politicians, businessmen and academics to discuss international issues.
Dayan, a member of the Peace Now movement in Israel, said the Washington summit, if not a total failure, was "not what we expected."

"Our prime minister refused to give any kind of date or commit himself to dates on the redeployment of (Israeli troops from) Hebron or any of the things that were demanded," she told a news conference.

President Bill Clinton called the summit with Netanyahu, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Jordan's King Hussein in an effort to rescue the Middle East peace process after an explosion of violence last week that took the lives of 57 Palestinians and 15 Israelis.
"We hope that as he (Netanyahu) goes home now, the mere fact that he has refused to set a timetable will not cause more bloodshed," Dayan said.
The summit ended on Wednesday with no deal on any Israeli-Palestinian dispute, but the two sides did agree to resume talks.
Aloni accused Israel's new government of turning "a political conflict into a religious war."

She said she had felt the summit would achieve more. "When he's (Netanyahu) coming back without a date, without clear answers, then he'll start the whole game and rhetoric again, that's what I'm afraid of," Aloni said.
Dayan said she did not think it was futile to bring the Middle Eastern leaders to Washington for the talks.
"I think it was very wise to take him (Netanyahu) away from what became his entourage of cheerleaders and bring him into a relatively objective environment in Washington," she said.

"I think he is going home with a very clear message, Mr. Netanyahu, and that's why it's not a total failure. He's going home with the understanding that the U.S. will not go along the line of Israel, right or wrong. There were very clear demands made on him," Dayan said.
Both Israeli politicians criticised Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole, who warned Clinton on Tuesday not to pressure Netanyahu.
"This is not the time for candidate Dole to stand up and criticise ... I would have liked to see him say the same as Clinton does and not to turn it into some kind of election issue," Dayan said.
